messages:
alex (AE): FYI — Prospect (Brightleaf) wants to sign this week but procurement flagged two things: they want Net-60 on the order form and they asked Legal to remove our indemnity cap. Can someone from legal/procurement advise?

marta (AM): Oof. Sales motion is at the finish line, but Net-60 is a hard ask from their finance team. Do we have flexibility on payment terms for pilot?

dina (Legal): Need to see the exact MSA/DPA redlines. Removing the indemnity cap is a non-starter without compensation or reciprocal language. Can you drop the redlined PDF?

alex (AE): Dropped the redline in the thread: https://files.redwood/internal/brightleaf/redline_v3.pdf — main edits are: indemnity removal, add EU data residency clause, and change governing law to their state. Also they attached an internal PO template.

sam (Procurement): If they require Net-60 we can accept for Dedicated customers with finance approval and a 2% fee or USC check. For Hosted we typically do Net-30. Is this a revenue > $200k ARR deal?
marta (AM): Widening the ask: it's a 12mo pilot at $60k committed. Might bump to $250k if POC goes well. Asking for Net-60 to align with their vendor payment cycle.

dina (Legal): Quick read: the indemnity clause they removed exposes us to unlimited liability for third-party claims. Proposed counter: keep mutual indemnities, cap at the greater of $1M or total fees, carve out IP indemnities. Paste of proposed text below:

```
Indemnity: Each party will indemnify the other for direct third-party claims arising from the indemnifying party's gross negligence or willful misconduct. The indemnified party's recovery shall be limited to direct damages up to the greater of (i) $1,000,000 or (ii) fees paid under the applicable Order Form in the prior twelve (12) months.
```

alex (AE): That looks reasonable. For commercial approval do we need escalations to finance or CRO?

sam (Procurement): Finance signoff required for Net-60 at this size. If Legal keeps our cap, Finance is more likely to OK Net-60. Otherwise they want upfront partial payment (50% upfront).

dina (Legal): Also, DPA: they added a clause forcing data residency to the EU for all EU users and on-premise logging retention. We can agree to EU data residency for EU tenants but need SOC/contract amendments for on-prem requirements. Suggest: accept EU residency for production data, exclude audit/hardware-level logging for Hosted.

marta (AM): They also insist on DocuSign routing to a central procurement email instead of the AE. Our e-sign vendor has a limit: if signature routing bypasses named signers, we need Legal to approve delegated signing authority. @esign-bot any automated routing notes?

esign-bot: Automations report: standard Order Form template supports signatory email override, but compliance flag will lock if more than 2 signers are changed. Manual exception requires Legal approval and a signed delegation form.

dina (Legal): I'll prepare a short delegation template and a counter-redline with the indemnity cap and residency language. If Finance approves Net-60 we can proceed; otherwise go back with 50% upfront. I can turn around the draft in ~3 hours.

sam (Procurement): I'll ping finance now. If they want a PO + Net-60, we must get an authorized signer list. Please request the procurement contact to CC their CFO on the PO.

alex (AE): I'll request CFO cc and ask if they can do 30 days on pilot, escalate for Net-60 if they insist.

marta (AM): Action items: (1) Dina to share counter-redline (2) Sam to confirm finance on Net-60/50% upfront (3) Alex to request CFO cc & confirm signer routing. ETA EOD.

dina (Legal): Counter-redline link when ready: https://files.redwood/internal/brightleaf/counter_v1.pdf. I'll include delegation template for e-sign exceptions.

esign-bot: Noted: once delegation template is signed, system will allow procurement routing without locking. Request ID: ESIGN-4872.

alex (AE): Thanks team — keeping customer warm. I told them we can likely sign this week pending the two approvals. :thumbsup:
